title: Autoscaler sensor glitch prevents warm-pool promotions causing tenant cold-starts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers experienced sustained high p95/p99 latency and token queueing over a 3-hour window on 2026-03-10. Root cause is a regression in the autoscaler "sensor" pipeline that feeds the warm-pool promotion logic. The sensor started producing zeros for prefix-hit metrics for a subset of tenants, which the debounce logic treated as 'no change' and therefore suppressed promotions to warm pools. Consequence: tenants remained in cold pools, lost KV cache benefits and batching efficiency; burst credits were consumed quickly and customers observed degraded throughput and elevated cost per token.

Impact: Customer escalations from two mid-market customers (AcmePay, ThaliaHealth) and internal SRE alerts. Affected ~14 reserved pools across us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Customer-impact: high.

Reproduction steps:
1) Create a reserved pool with mixed steady/peak traffic (simulated via perf-runner).
2) Instrument prefix_hit_rate export, then deploy autoscaler sensor with metric rename (prefix_hit_rate_pct).
3) Trigger traffic bursts; observe warm-pool promotion counter not incrementing and warm_nodes remains low despite rising queue length.

Initial mitigation taken:
- At 2026-03-10T17:23Z SRE applied manual warm promotions for impacted tenants using admin API to restore KV cache and reduce latency.
- Temporarily increased reserved headroom by +2 nodes per affected pool to absorb burst for 8 hours.
- Notified customers (AcmePay, ThaliaHealth) and provided traffic/latency dashboard snapshots and ETA for a permanent fix.

Root cause (analysis so far):
- A metrics refactor in runtime-1.21 renamed "prefix_hit_rate" -> "prefix_hit_rate_pct" and changed formatting to include a percent sign in the exporter for a small subset of models.
- The autoscaler sensor parser expects a numeric float and trims non-digit characters; a locale-aware string->float routine introduced earlier in the week incorrectly returned 0 when a trailing '%' is present (it didn't strip the % in the new path).
- Because the sensor returned 0 for that metric, the debounce controller treated the metric as 'unchanged' (edge-case in debounce math) and suppressed promotion signals when combined with a new debounce window optimization shipped in runtime-1.21.
- Interaction with burst accounting: blocked promotions meant tenants consumed burst capacity instead of steady capacity, so burst budgets drained faster and triggered fallback throttles.

Immediate fix implemented:
- Hotfix PR (see comments) restores backwards-compatible parsing: strip non-numeric suffixes and fall back to previous metric name if new metric absent.
- Reverted the problematic debounce optimization in the autoscaler controller for the warm-pool path to avoid further suppression while we validate sensor stability.

Planned rollout and testing:
- Canary deploy hotfix to us-west-2 on 2026-03-13 to 10% of reserved pools for 2 hours with synthetic and tenant shadow traffic.
- Monitor: warm_node_count, prefix_hit_rate (old and new), promotion_event_count, queue_length, burst_budget_consumption, and p99 latency.
- If stable, progressive rollout to eu-central-1 and remaining pools over 24 hours.

Postmortem action items (next steps):
- Create unit+integration tests for metric parsing that include percent-suffixed strings and locale variants.
- Add telemetry to track metric rename mismatches and emit a warning alert when sensor falls back to default-zero more than 1% of the time.
- Update rollout checklist: any runtime metric rename must include autoscaler sensor integration test and an opt-in experiment before full rollout.
- Add a dedicated SLO and alert: "warm-pool promotion rate" should not drop >30% relative to baseline.
- Customer remediation: offer ThaliaHealth one month of reserved-credit as goodwill; schedule technical review with AcmePay for configurable warm-pool thresholds.

Notes: This ticket spans both runtime and autoscaler controller teams. Coordination with Product is required for customer comms and compensation approvals.
